A.name: Avery Lindgren
A.platform: Hold Halden until our hidden pontoon bridge is ready, then evacuate the 6,000 civilians and the brigade by nightfall while destroying the original crossing to block Vostra's advance.

strategies.text: Appeal to the moral weight of the civilians and the strategic timing of the allied aid vote to sway members against Reese's retreat.
I am appealing to the council's sense of justice and long-term reputation by reframing the immediate tactical risk as a necessary price for saving civilians and securing future aid.
Appeal to the council's duty to protect civilians by framing the delay as a guaranteed rescue window rather than a dangerous gamble.

B.name: Reese Calder
B.platform: Execute an immediate fighting withdrawal across the bridge tonight, destroy the crossing, and redeploy reserves to secure Mirov.

strategies.text: Emphasize the mathematical certainty of annihilation if we stay versus the high probability of survival if we go, forcing the council to choose between pride and survival.
I am attacking the feasibility of their pontoon bridge timeline and emphasizing that immediate action saves civilians now rather than gambling on a future rescue.
Emphasize the fatal flaw in Avery's reliance on a completed bridge under surveillance to counter her moral appeal with hard probabilities of failure.

transcript.name: Avery Lindgren
transcript.speech: Imagine six-year-old Elara in Orsk, left behind as we fled her village; that is not who we are. Reese proposes a withdrawal tonight, but our engineers can build a hidden pontoon bridge in four days, doubling supply capacity if we hold the high ground one last week. Vostra's intelligence says they attack within seventy-two hours; that is exactly our window to double our supplies and evacuate safely before their drones spot us. We fight for justice, not just lines on a map. Holding now protects the elderly who cannot walk out in the cold, denies Vostra a propaganda victory before the aid vote, and secures Mirov more effectively by blowing the bridge behind us. Let us choose courage that saves lives without surrendering our future.

transcript.name: Reese Calder
transcript.speech: We must withdraw Halden tonight. Vostra has massed fifteen thousand troops against our three thousand eight hundred; holding is a losing calculation that guarantees total destruction of the brigade. A night withdrawal saves eighty percent of our soldiers and evacuates most civilians before artillery hits, whereas standing ground means losing the entire force and freezing six thousand people to death. Blowing the bridge immediately denies Vostra access to Mirov for at least three weeks, buying us time to receive allied air defenses. Sacrificing a fortified position is not cowardice; it is the only arithmetic that preserves our fighting capacity and prevents a strategic collapse of our eastern flank.

transcript.name: Avery Lindgren
transcript.speech: Reese, you speak of arithmetic while ignoring the human cost. Your plan sacrifices six thousand civilians to save a brigade that can be saved with time. Yes, we face higher risks holding Halden, but your immediate withdrawal leaves the elderly behind and grants Vostra a propaganda victory before our aid vote. If we withdraw tonight, the hidden pontoon bridge remains unfinished; if we hold four days, it doubles our survival capacity. We are not just defending ground; we are proving that Kaldmark does not abandon its most vulnerable when facing overwhelming odds. Let us use this narrow window to secure a victory of will, save our soldiers through superior logistics, and deny Vostra the moral high ground they crave.

transcript.name: Reese Calder
transcript.speech: Your arithmetic on survival capacity is flawed. Blowing the bridge tonight leaves exactly zero evacuation windows for the 6,000 civilians currently inside, freezing them while Vostra's artillery prepares. Your plan relies on engineers finishing a pontoon in four days under drone surveillance; historical data from Orsk shows we have no guarantee of safe passage if that first window fails. Holding increases expected deaths linearly because supplies run out in nine days regardless of morale. We are trading certain, immediate starvation for speculative future rescue. If we retreat tonight, we control the bridge's destruction timing to deny Mirov immediately while evacuating under cover of darkness before Vostra detects our movement. The moral imperative is saving those who cannot walk today, not gambling their lives on a construction project that may never be finished.

transcript.name: Avery Lindgren
transcript.speech: Reese argues for immediate retreat, but his plan leaves six thousand civilians behind in freezing darkness tonight. He fears our engineer project will fail, yet history shows Vostra breaks ceasefires just like Orsk; waiting gives us a guaranteed window, not a gamble. If we pull now, we surrender the moral high ground and grant them a propaganda victory that halts future aid. My plan holds the line long enough to complete the hidden bridge, then evacuates everyone under cover of night before blowing both crossings. We prove Kaldmark does not abandon its most vulnerable. Let us choose a victory that saves every life, secures our soldiers, and denies them the moral high ground they crave.

transcript.name: Reese Calder
transcript.speech: Avery's plan assumes a miracle: finishing a hidden bridge in four days under drone surveillance. History from Orsk proves Vostra breaks ceasefires, making that window nonexistent. By holding tonight, we gamble the immediate safety of six thousand civilians on speculative logistics. If the bridge fails, they freeze or die before our artillery runs out. Your plan risks total destruction of both the brigade and the civilians for a propaganda victory we cannot afford. My plan executes tonight. We evacuate the majority safely, destroy the crossings to secure Mirov immediately, and redeploy reserves while retaining our fighting capacity. This is not cowardice; it is the only arithmetic that prevents total collapse.
